Row.Text: Strategic Resources That Matter

Strategic resources matter again. A unit that draws on Horses, Iron, Niter, Oil, Coal or Rubber fights weaker and trains slower while its owner holds none of that resource, and every copy still adds the game's own bonus. Lose your last copy and the penalty comes back a turn later. Past six copies the count keeps adding strength. Two game setup options set the penalty and switch the late bonus. Single-player. In multiplayer, losing a resource does not bring the penalty back until that player gains a resource.

Strategic Resources Past Six
The game's bonus of +1 Combat Strength per copy of a strategic resource stops at six copies. With this on, units gain +1 more at 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20 copies.

Strategic Resources That Matter

A military unit that draws on {LOC_RESOURCE_HORSES_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_IRON_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME} or {LOC_RESOURCE_RUBBER_NAME} fights weaker and trains slower while its owner holds no copy of that resource. Nothing is forbidden: every unit can still be trained and upgraded as in the base game.
Without a copy

A unit short of its resource has less Combat Strength, on each strength it has (melee, and ranged and bombard where it has them), and its city puts less Production toward training it. The {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_NAME} option in game setup sets how much:

[B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LIGHT}:[/B] -2 Combat Strength, 20% less Production.[N][B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_STANDARD}[/B] (the default): -3 Combat Strength, 33% less Production, so the unit takes half as long again to train.[N][B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_HARSH}:[/B] -5 Combat Strength, 50% less Production, twice as long to train.[N][B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_OFF}:[/B] no penalty.
The combat preview shows the penalty as a line of its own, such as "-3 Unsupplied: no {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}", and the unit panel says so under the unit's stats.
What counts as a copy

A copy is a strategic resource on the map that you hold: on a tile of yours that carries the improvement for that resource (the one your city builds when it grows onto the tile), or imported over a trade route from another civilization's settlement, from the turn the route lands.
A resource granted off the map, with no tile behind it, does not count.
Losing a copy

A new copy lifts the penalty the moment it arrives. A copy that goes away, by pillage, by a tile changing hands or in any other way, brings the penalty back one turn later, for you and for the AI players alike.
A war with a trade partner ends the route: the copies it brought are gone at once, and so is their protection. While a player holds at least one copy, its units have no penalty.
Past six copies

The game gives +1 Combat Strength per copy, up to six copies. With the {LOC_SR_SETUP_LATE_CURVE_NAME} option on (the default), more copies keep adding: +1 Combat Strength at 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20 copies, on the units the game's per-copy bonus covers. The combat preview shows it as one line beside the game's own, such as "+1 {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}: 8 or more copies".
Which units need what
A civilization's unique unit needs what the unit it replaces needs.

[B]{LOC_AGE_EXPLORATION_NAME}[/B][N]{LOC_RESOURCE_HORSES_NAME}: cavalry (Courser, Knight, Lancer and their unique versions)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_IRON_NAME}: infantry from the second tier (Man-At-Arms, Pikeman and their unique versions)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}: siege (Catapult, Trebuchet, Bombard, Hwacha) and heavy warships from the second tier (Carrack, Galleon and their unique versions)

[B]{LOC_AGE_MODERN_NAME}[/B][N]{LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}: artillery (Field Cannon, Field Gun, AT Gun, Mortar, Howitzer, Assault Gun)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME}: armour (Landship, Tank and their unique versions) and battleships (Dreadnought, Battleship and their unique versions)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME}: light warships (Ironclad, Cruiser, Destroyer, Barbary Corsair)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_RUBBER_NAME}: aircraft

Free of any requirement: the Warrior line and the Scout, ranged infantry (Archer, Crossbowman, Arquebusier), the Cog and the Ship of the Line, the Cuirassier, the Submarine, and Modern infantry, so every player can always defend.
